newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal wants convertible bonds launch.
newsitem.headline: Universal wants convertible bonds launch.

text.p: Polish trading firm Universal SA wants its general shareholders meeting on October 30 to vote on the postponed convertible bonds issue and new share issue ex-rights, the company said in a statement.
It said it wanted to increase its share capital by 60 million, but gave no further details. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
The firm earlier said it wanted to offer 810 five-year, 12 percent convertible bonds with a face value of 100,000 zlotys at par in a private placement to no more than 300 selected investors.
It said the bonds could be converted into the company's stock from April 1, 1997, until December 31, 2001.
Each bond would be exchanged for 10,000 new common shares with a par value of five zlotys each.
